senses.gloss: छिद् [cf. σχίζω, σχίδη &c.; Lat. scindo; Goth. skeida.]
2. छिद् mfn. ifc. (Pāṇ. iii, 2, 61) cutting, cutting off, cutting through, splitting, piercing, MBh. vii, 4656 (cf. उख-च्छि॑द्, केश-, पक्ष-, मर्म-, वन-, हृदय-)
destroying, annihilating, removing, MBh. v, 1809; Hariv. 4774; Bhartṛ.; BhP. (cf. दर्प-, दुःख-, पङ्क-, भव-)
छिद् m. the divisor, denominator
छिद् f. the cutting off (with gen.), Bālar. viii, 75
‘annihilation of (in comp.)’, see भव-.
छिद mfn. ifc. ‘cutting off’, see मातृक-
छिदा f. (g. भिदादि) the cutting off (ifc.), HYog. ii, 96.
छिदक m. ‘thunderbolt’ or ‘diamond’ (cf. Rājat. iv, 51), L.
छिदि an axe, Uṇ. iv, 120
छिदिर m. id., i, 52
a sword, ib.
fire, L.
a rope, cord, L.
छिदुर mf(आ, Pāṇ. iii, 2, 162)n. cutting, dividing, W.
easily breaking, Ragh. xvi, 62; Hcar. vi
extinguishing, Śiś. vi, 8
decreasing, Vām. v, 2, 40
annihilating (ifc.), ib.
hostile, L.
roguish, L.
छिदुरेतर mfn. not breaking, strong, Naiṣ. vii, 64.
छिद्र॑ mf(आ)n. torn asunder, RV. i, 162, 20
containing holes, pierced, KātyŚr. xv ff.; R. i, 73, 20; Suśr. v, 1, 43

छिद्र॑ n. a hole, slit, cleft, opening, VS.; TS. i, vi; KātyŚr.; Lāṭy.; Kauś.; Mn. &c. (दैव-कृत, ‘opening or hole made by nature’, the cartilage of the ear, pupil of the eye, Suśr.; ˚द्रं √ दा, ‘to yield an opening or free access’, BhP. v, 6, 4)
defect, fault, blemish, imperfection, infirmity, weak point, foible, MBh. &c.
(in astrol.) the 8th lunar mansion, VarBṛ.; Laghuj. i, 17
the number ‘nine’ (there being 9 openings in the body), Sūryas. ii, 18
the lower regions, Gal. (cf. अ॑-, कर्ण-, कृत-, गृह-, निश्-, महा-).
छिद्र—कर्ण mfn. having the ears bored, Pāṇ. vi, 3, 115.
छिद्र—ता f. ‘perforatedness’, the (air's, आकाशस्य) being pervaded by everything, MBh. xii, 9137.
छिद्र—दर्शन mfn. ‘exhibiting deficiencies’, only अ-च्छ्˚, faultless, MBh. vi, 384 and 402
छिद्र—दर्शन m. ‘=’ ˚र्शिन् N. of a (Brāhman changed into a) Cakra-vāka, Hariv. 1216
छिद्र—दर्शिन् mfn. observing deficiencies, 1265
छिद्र—दर्शिन् m. = ˚र्शन, (q.v. at end).
छिद्र—दातृ-त्व n. the (air's, आकाशस्य) yielding openings or access to everything, BhP. iii, 26, 34.
छिद्र—पिप्पली f. Scindapsus officinalis, Gal.
छिद्र—वैदेही f. id., L.
छिद्रांश m. ‘having perforated parts’, reed, Gal.
छिद्रात्मन् mfn. one who exposes his weak points, MBh. xii, 11345.
छिद्रानुसंधानिन् mfn. looking out for faults or flaws, W.
छिद्रानुसारिन् mfn. id., W.
छिद्रान्तर् m. ‘internally hollow’, reed, L.
छिद्रान्वित mfn. having weak points, Pañcat. iii, 37.
छिद्रान्वेषण n. searching for faults, W.
छिद्रान्वेषिन् m. = ˚नुसंधानिन्, W.
छिद्रा-फल n. a thorn-apple, L.
छिद्रोदर n. N. of a disease of the abdomen, Car. vi, 18,
छिद्रोदरिन् mfn. affected with ˚र, ib.
छिद्रय Nom. ˚यति, to perforate, Kād. vi, 550.
छिद्रापय Nom. ˚यति id., Vop.
छिद्रित mfn. perforated, Kād. v, 1071; Prab. v, 30, Sch.
छिद्रिन् mfn. having holes (a tooth), Suśr. ii, 16, 27.
छिद्वर mfn. = छित्त्व्˚, W.
